text: Khatia Dekanoidze - If we look at what is happening in Armenia, we will see that the function Georgia had—to be the leader of the region—no longer exists. Because of Ivanishvili’s crime and the “anti-Georgian Dream,” Georgia is losing this function (06.05.2026, 12:00)

Today, Ivanishvili and the “anti-Georgian Dream” have deprived Georgia of the function of long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have deprived the Georgian people of the opportunity for prosperity and enrichment, and of the opportunity for European integration. This is a historical crime,” said Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the “United National Movement.”

He congratulated the public 22 years ago, on May 6, on the “liberation of Adjara from Russian and despotic rule” and noted that it was on this day that a new chapter in Georgia’s history began, one that implied the region’s leadership.

“Congratulations on one of the most outstanding dates in Georgia’s recent history — the return of Adjara to Georgia. Twenty-two years ago, on exactly May 6, one of the most important events in Georgia’s recent history took place, when Adjara returned to the heart of Georgia, was freed from Russian rule, freed from the rule of a despot, and, together with President Mikheil Saakashvili, his team, and many ardent patriots, a very important ascent began. And yes, Georgia began a new chapter, one that meant regional leadership, development in technology and education, in the context of the expansion of Eastern Europe, in the context of strategic partnership with the United States — which was truly the historical mission of our nation. It was a day when we moved to a completely different path of state development, and our team managed to ensure that Georgia truly gained the function of a regional leader. Today, Ivanishvili and the ‘anti-Georgian Dream’ have deprived Georgia of the function of long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have deprived the Georgian people of the opportunity for prosperity and enrichment, of the opportunity for Eurointegration. This is a historical crime, and if we look at what is happening in our neighboring Armenia — and I want to wish them great success — you will see that the function Georgia had, to be a regional leader and to have many sustainable peace projects, no longer exists. The developments in Armenia in recent days are not only political support from the European Union, the United States, or Canada for our neighbors; these are investment projects that truly imply long-term peace. We had many such projects, including the Batumi Technological University, in which Mikheil Saakashvili, who is today a political prisoner, was directly involved in its development and construction, and I myself am very proud that I took part in the construction of this technological university. This university was supposed to become truly one of Georgia’s important hubs for education, technology, new communication systems, and the transition to a new stage of education. What was happening in Armenia is not only political support; it is economic support that ensures long-term peace. Every person who was involved in the most important stages of Georgia’s development is now watching how the country is losing this function because of Ivanishvili’s crime, because of the ‘anti-Georgian Dream.’ The 400 billion in investment, military-technological cooperation with France and the United States, energy security projects, the most important new corridor that the European Commission, the European Union, the United States, and Canada are now talking about, the huge investments that are one of the most important areas of peace, sustainable development, and progress — Georgia is losing all of this,” Dekanoidze said.
